title: AI Weekly Brief
label: Editorial blueprint
summary: A public, high-signal briefing designed to turn the week’s AI noise into a short list of developments worth discussing.

review.note: These demonstration cards explain the editorial standard. Scheduled collection is active, but only a reviewed issue may replace them.

sections.title: The Week in AI
sections.description: The few strategic developments that deserve executive attention.

stories.title: Signal over volume is the core editorial rule
stories.summary: A real issue will lead with the developments most likely to change a decision, strategy, or operating assumption—not the stories with the loudest launch cycle.
stories.whyItMatters: Keeps the briefing concise enough to read and consequential enough to discuss.

stories.title: Approval protects the current issue
stories.summary: Every Friday or on-demand refresh creates a separate draft. The approved briefing stays intact until a reviewed draft is promoted successfully.
stories.whyItMatters: A partial refresh or weak news week can never overwrite a trusted issue.

sections.title: Models & Capabilities
sections.description: Material releases and capability shifts, separated from routine product churn.

stories.title: Capability shifts must clear a materiality bar
stories.summary: Model coverage should show what changed, how credible the evidence is, and whether the change alters practical choices for DFP.
stories.whyItMatters: Turns release notes into decision context instead of repeating vendor claims.

sections.title: For Builders
sections.description: Useful tools, repositories, and implementation lessons—kept to a deliberate share.

stories.title: Practical coverage earns its place by being useful
stories.summary: Builder stories should offer something a team can evaluate, test, or apply. Novelty alone is not enough to make the cut.
stories.whyItMatters: Preserves an executive-ready brief while giving delivery teams a practical next move.

sections.title: Research Watch
sections.description: A small research selection chosen for consequence, not paper count.

stories.title: Research is selected for the direction it reveals
stories.summary: Only work that clarifies a meaningful capability, risk, limitation, or technical direction should enter the weekly brief.
stories.whyItMatters: Keeps research connected to implications rather than treating publication volume as importance.
